_meta.indication: Asclera (polidocanol) is a sclerosing agent indicated to treat uncomplicated spider veins (varicose veins ≤1 mm in diameter) and uncomplicated reticular veins (varicose veins 1 to 3 mm in diameter) in the lower extremity

pivotal_trials.trial_name: EASI trial (Efficacy and safety of Aethoxysklerol compared to Sodium tetra-decyl sulfate and Isotonic saline (placebo) for the treatment of reticular veins and spider veins)
pivotal_trials.phase: Not explicitly stated; a placebo- and comparator-controlled, double-blind, multicenter pivotal trial
pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo- and comparator-controlled trial conducted at 19 centers in Germany
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with uncomplicated spider veins (≤1 mm) or reticular veins (1 to 3 mm) in the lower extremity; predominantly female, ages 19 to 70 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary effectiveness endpoint: improvement of veins judged by a blinded panel from digital images at 12 weeks, rated on a 5-point scale
pivotal_trials.n: 338 patients treated (Asclera/polidocanol 180 [0.5% spider N=94, 1% reticular N=86], STS 1% N=105, placebo N=53)
pivotal_trials.result: Digital photograph improvement score at 12 weeks: polidocanol 4.5 ± 0.7 vs placebo 2.2 ± 0.7 (p < 0.0001). Treatment success (grade 4-5) at 12 weeks: polidocanol 95% vs placebo 8% (p<0.0001)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions are mild local injection-site reactions occurring at least 3% more frequently than placebo: injection site haematoma (42% vs 19% placebo), irritation (41% vs 30%), discoloration (38% vs 4%), and pain (24% vs 9%). Serious risk of anaphylactic reactions, some fatal, reported with polidocanol use.
target_moa: Polidocanol is a sclerosing agent that locally damages the endothelium of blood vessels; platelets aggregate at the damage site, a network of platelets, cellular debris, and fibrin occludes the vessel, and the occluded vein is replaced with connective fibrous tissue

advisory_committee.vote: Not referred to an advisory committee because the clinical study design was acceptable and the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues

summary.text: ASCLERA (polidocanol) NDA 21-201 was a Priority review application; the earlier 2003 submission received a non-approvable letter on 08/02/2004, and the sponsor submitted the current NDA on 07/21/2008 with the pivotal EASI trial to address those issues, leading to approval on a standard (non-accelerated) full-approval pathway with a postmarketing requirement to monitor anaphylaxis and death.

The applicant previously submitted data to the agency under NDA 21-201 in 2003 for consideration by the agency to grant marketing approval of polidocanol for the treatment of varicose veins of the lower extremities.
On 08/02/2004, the Office of Drug Evaluation III issued a non-approvable letter because

NDA 21-201 and related IND 35,139 were transferred to the Division of Cardiovascular and Renal Products in May, 2005. After FDA evaluation of a special protocol assessment, the sponsor submitted the current NDA on 07/21/2008 addressing the issues stated in the non-approvable letter. The submission consists of:

requirement.text: PMR #1612-1: An assessment of spontaneous reports of anaphylaxis or death associated with Asclera (polidocanol), submitting a yearly report analyzing spontaneous adverse event reports describing anaphylaxis or death, with cases submitted as 15-day reports

citations.quote: - An assessment of spontaneous reports of anaphylaxis or death associated with Asclera (polidocanol). Following approval, and according to the following timetable, submit a yearly report (containing both interval-based and comprehensive data) analyzing spontaneous adverse event reports received that describes anaphylaxis or death. Cases of anaphylaxis or death should be submitted as 15-day reports.
